articles.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Gordon leads options to replace Achane for Week 4 and beyond
articles.description: Eric Karabell lists who he thinks are the top available players worth adding for the week ahead.
articles.body:
Each Monday, before the current NFL week ends, we will identify players worthy of your attention who are available in at least 50% of ESPN standard leagues. Things change quickly for player valuation and roles each week in the NFL, and free agency is a critical way to acquire players. We are here to help!

Top pickup options at every position

Looking for the top recommendation at each skill position? Look no further! Here are the players to target heading into Week 3, along with their current roster percentages and a recommendation of how much of your free agent budget (FAB) you should consider using for your bid. 

Sam Darnold, QB, Seahawks (rostered in 33.9%, 5% of your FAB)

Darnold (glute) missed most of Week 1 and all of Week 2, but he sure looked healthy in Sunday's shootout against the Washington Commanders. Game score and a challenged run game dictated myriad passes, and Darnold completed 31 out of 45 attempts for a career-high 379 yards and four touchdowns. He also tossed a pair of interceptions, one of which was returned for a score.

Immeasurably aided by dominating WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who is off to one of the greatest starts ever, Darnold might match his success from last season, when he surpassed 4,000 passing yards, threw 25 TD passes and mattered in fantasy. The Seattle Seahawks host the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4.

Ollie Gordon II, RB, Dolphins (1.1%, 12% FAB)

Gordon, a second-year Oklahoma State product who averaged only 2.8 yards per his 70 carries last season, replaced an injured De'Von Achane (knee) during Week 3's action and scored 14.5 points. Gordon wasn't efficient, but getting 20 touches and scoring a touchdown often masks inefficiency. With Achane reportedly done for the season, Gordon is next up, although Jaylen Wright might have a role, too.

Keenan Allen, WR, Colts (23.8%, 7% FAB)

Allen, second among active players in receptions behind Travis Kelce, was one of three Indianapolis Colts to earn at least nine targets Sunday, but he was the one who scored the team's touchdown. In addition, teammates WR Josh Downs and TE Tyler Warren are already rostered in most leagues. Allen is not, but with Alec Pierce (heel) on IR, he now has opportunity. Allen isn't close to the threat he was as recently as 2023, but he did catch 81 passes for last season's Chargers (for only 777 yards), so perhaps he can do that again.

Kenyon Sadiq, TE, Jets (33.5%, 10% FAB)

Sadiq, selected 16th in the draft out of Oregon, scored a short rushing TD in Week 1, but he totaled only six targets and 38 receiving yards through two weeks, failing to excite potential investors. They might be excited now, after Sadiq caught seven passes for 105 yards and a 24-yard TD on Sunday. Sadiq is strong and fast and is a potential top-10 fantasy tight end if he gets the targets. He should from now on.

articles.headline: Sources: Giants acquire QB J.J. McCarthy in trade with Vikings
articles.description: The Giants are trading for Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy, sending a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to Minnesota in exchange for the former first-round pick, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.
articles.body:
The New York Giants are trading for Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.

The Giants are sending a 2027 fifth-round pick to Minnesota in exchange for McCarthy, the sources said.

McCarthy, picked by the Vikings with the No. 10 pick in the 2024 draft, was the third string quarterback in Minnesota behind starter Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz.

Giants coach John Harbaugh said after Sunday's victory over the Tennessee Titans that Jameis Winston would remain the Giants' starter even if the team added another quarterback.

Winston became the starter following the knee injury to Jaxson Dart, who is out for at least the rest of the regular season after undergoing surgery to repair the meniscus and MCL in his left knee on Friday.

McCarthy was coached by Jim Harbaugh at Michigan and now will be coached by John Harbaugh in the NFL with the Giants.

McCarthy lost his starting job with the Vikings in training camp to veteran Kyler Murray and was demoted to third string after an ankle injury kept him out of the Vikings' final preseason game. His career with the Vikings ended with 10 starts, and his departure comes at an age -- 23 years and 9 months -- that makes him younger than most of the NFL's quarterbacks who were selected in the 2026 draft.

But a combination of injuries, poor throwing mechanics and immaturity left the Vikings unwilling to wait on the possibility of future development -- making him one of the biggest draft busts in team history. McCarthy is one of four Vikings first-round picks -- along Lewis Cine, Dimitrius Underwood and Leo Hayden -- to play 10 or fewer games for the team, according to the Elias Sports Bureau.

Among all NFL teams, McCarthy is one of four quarterbacks in the past 25 years to start 10 or fewer games for the team that drafted them, joining Paxton Lynch, Trey Lance and Johnny Manziel, per the Elias Sports Bureau. The list does not include Eli Manning and Philip Rivers, who were traded for each other shortly after being selected in the 2004 draft.

McCarthy's final appearance in a Vikings uniform, an Aug. 22 preseason game against the Baltimore Ravens, encapsulated his tenure. After misfiring on two throws to open receivers in the end zone, McCarthy suffered a mild ankle sprain during a hit in the pocket. He got up from the ground slowly, walked to the sideline and coach Kevin O'Connell ended his day earlier than scheduled.

Winston has struggled since replacing the injured Dart, completing just 51% of his pass attempts for 229 yards with no touchdowns and an interceptions.

The Giants defeated the Titans 12-7 at MetLife Stadium, despite not scoring a touchdown, to improve to 2-1 this season. 

ESPN's Kevin Seifert contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Giannis confident in what he can offer to overhauled Heat
articles.description: Giannis Antetokounmpo has no doubt about his potential as he enters the next stage of his career following a blockbuster trade to the Heat, saying he can still "dominate the game" as one of the best players in the world.
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo has no doubt about his potential as he enters the next stage of his career following a blockbuster trade to the Miami Heat.

"I really do believe that, if not the best, I'm one of the best players in the world," Antetokounmpo said Monday at Heat media day. "I know when I'm at my best, when I'm locked in, when my body is right, I really do believe that I can dominate the game and I can impact the game in both ways, offensively and defensively. I think I've shown it over the years."

The two-time MVP who led the Milwaukee Bucks to an NBA title in 2021 officially starts the next chapter of his career Tuesday, when the Heat open training camp in Boca Raton, Florida. He was the centerpiece of a massive roster restructuring by Miami this summer, one that saw the Heat add Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, Bobby Portis and Tim Hardaway Jr., among others, to a core led by Bam Adebayo, Andrew Wiggins, Pelle Larsson and Davion Mitchell.

"This is all new for me," Antetokounmpo said. "I'm trying to learn defense. I'm learning offenses. I am trying to fit in the locker room with new faces. I'm trying to be able to play with players that I've never played before. It's all new for me. It's exciting.

"I know that I'm going to put in the work. Succeed or fail, I'm going to fail by working or succeed by working. And the goal is to win a championship. That's the goal."

The Kaseya Center, the Heat's home arena, is a construction site these days. Dozens of workers in hard hats, orange reflective vests and steel-toed boots are all over the building, putting the finishing touches on new club spaces and other amenities that will greet fans in a couple of weeks.

Seems fitting that the team has gone through a refurbishment of sorts as well.

"I feel like there's a synergy from a lot of people in the building about this opportunity and the appropriate time," Heat coach Erik Spoelstra said. "Some things in this league really are about alignment. And then we'll see how it all plays out once we get into the competition and the games and all that."

Antetokounmpo entered the NBA in 2013. His career totals to date: 21,531 points, 8,882 rebounds and 4,484 assists. The point and rebound totals are both fifth best in the NBA over that span, while the assist total is 13th best.

Those numbers are just part of the reason why the Heat consider him to still be one of the five best players in the NBA.

"We brought him here for a reason. He's here for a reason," Spoelstra said. "We want him to establish himself as in that conversation of being the best player in the league, and that can be debated in a lot of different ways. But we're not bringing him here to take a step back, so we'll try to maximize his strengths as much as we can and get him as comfortable as possible."

articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Tuesday as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association will join them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams Tuesday.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 28

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant

Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's Media Day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. ...I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also added that veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing this season.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's Media Day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. ... Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team

Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss

After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season

After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

articles.headline: Warriors' Kristaps Porzingis out with 'health issue'
articles.description: Kristaps Porzingis will miss the start of Warriors training camp because of a health issue.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- The Golden State Warriors will be without starting center Kristaps Porzingis to open training camp because of a "health issue," general manager Mike Dunleavy announced Monday.

The Warriors are keeping the details private and calling Porzingis' absence indefinite. He will not travel with the team to Hawai'i, meaning he will miss at least the first four practices and the preseason opener against the LA Clippers next Sunday in Honolulu.

"I'm not marking him down as being out to start the season or anything like that," Dunleavy said. "He's just not available this week."

This has been a recurring issue for Porzingis, who has missed a combined 90 games the last two regular seasons primarily because of a mysterious health problem that emerged after he experienced a prolonged upper respiratory viral illness while with the Boston Celtics in late February 2025.

Porzingis missed 10 of his first 11 games with the Warriors after they acquired him from the Atlanta Hawks at last February's deadline but did then return and appear in 16 of the final 21 games.

That, in part, motivated the Warriors to bring Porzingis back this summer on a two-year, $40 million deal, guaranteeing only $3 million in the second season to maintain flexibility next summer.

There was internal optimism about how Porzingis looked this summer. He was in the team's San Francisco facility and on the court in the last week and appeared to be cleared for training camp before Dunleavy received a call Sunday night about Porzingis' latest health issue.

"He's been participating in everything," Dunleavy said. "It just kind of popped up."

The Warriors are already without starting wings Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody to enter the season. Both are in the middle stages of extended rehab for serious knee injuries.

"We feel comfortable with everything [about Porzingis' status]," Dunleavy said. "Disappointed that he won't be out there [when training camp starts Tuesday], but it's early, so don't want to overreact to anything."

articles.headline: AJ Dybantsa named cover athlete for 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball
articles.description: The Washington Wizards star began collecting cards this year and will be the cover athlete of 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball.
articles.body:
Fresh off being the top pick of the 2026 NBA draft, AJ Dybantsa was named cover athlete of 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball, the company announced on Monday. Pre orders are set to be available on Oct. 6. 

The Washington Wizards rookie never imagined being on a Topps cover, he told ESPN. 

"Topps has been in the business for such a long time, putting out cards before I was born," the 19-year-old told ESPN. "So the fact that I'm a cover athlete, I don't take it lightly. I'm very grateful and appreciative for it."

(Image courtesy of Topps)

Dybantsa is the second consecutive top overall pick to be the cover athlete, with Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg getting the honors last year. Flagg and Dybantsa are both from the New England area: Flagg from Newport, Maine, and Dybantsa from Boston.

Their shared region is something the Wizards forward pointed out when reflecting on following Flagg up.

"Us both being from New England, just putting on for our side of the map," he said. "The northeast doesn't get a lot of love, other than tristate, in my opinion. So us both being from New England, trying to put on for the cities, it feels good."

The Topps Flagship Basketball boasts 20 cards per box with 12 cards per pack. The collection is headlined by a strong 2026 draft class. Following Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson went No. 2 to the Utah Jazz, Cameron Boozer went No. 3 to the Memphis Grizzlies and the Chicago Bulls took Caleb Wilson at No. 4.

Autographed cards of rookies, as well as of veterans and legends, are included. There are also new inserts, including a first-ever Gold one-of-one All Kings parallel, according to Fanatics.

And Dybantsa is the face of it, following a year where his interest in collecting cards grew. When he started signing cards, he started collecting, too, and even has two of himself -- one he bought at Fanatics Fest in July and the other he pulled randomly.

Once the Wizards selected him with the top pick in June, Dybantsa walked on stage, shook NBA commissioner Adam Silver's hand and headed to ESPN's set for an interview. By the time he took his seat, his first NBA rookie card was made. Dybantsa then signed it live on air.

"It was crazy. I don't even know how they did it, to be honest," he said. "I just took the picture, walked the stage. I don't know how they got the card that fast, but it was super exciting. ... I hope to get it one day, but someone else might."

Being a Topps cover athlete should presumably give Dybantsa the upper hand on securing the card. It would only be appropriate, especially since his interest in having his own card has intensified.

Attending Fanatics Fest added to that desire.

"You end up going to that little area where they sell all the cards. And then you just have people bidding, people bidding for my card and it's like now I want to get into it," he said. "I want to collect my own card. So the dude was actually able to help me out and get my first signed card."
